subject: Pilot supplement pricing & ops playbook request
messages:
From: Ari Shah <ari@sparkfund.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Morales <kate@pilotlabs.io>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on pilot supplement credits and billing conversion

Ben — thanks for the demo last week. We run a small accelerator and are planning a set of pilot supplements (one-off free credits for cohort finalists) to encourage integrations. Two quick asks: 1) are those credits treated as promotional (write-off) or do they look like deferred revenue for accounting purposes, and 2) can they be converted to an onboarding discount if a team converts to Dedicated within 60 days?

I attached a one-page ask and a short usage sample to show consumption patterns. Would appreciate a short ops/playbook we can reference when we introduce this to our partners.

Thanks — Ari
SparkFund
[Attachment: sparkfund_pilot_ask.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Shah <ari@sparkfund.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on pilot supplement credits and billing conversion

Thanks Ari — good, pragmatic questions. Short answers up front: our default is to treat small promotional credits as marketing/promotional discounts (not deferred revenue) but there are edge cases where finance prefers an escrow/deferral treatment. Conversion to a Dedicated onboarding discount is supported but needs clear guardrails (time window, per-account cap, and one-time conversion).

Marissa + Irene — can you confirm the standard guardrails and share an internal playbook we can surface to SparkFund? I attached their quarter usage sample (usage_report_Q2.csv) so you can see the mix. If we need a formal exception (e.g., convert credits > $25k), flag the approval path and stakeholders.

Ari — I’ll loop back with a concise ops playbook and the recommended tax/accounting framing. If it helps, we can do a 20-minute sync tomorrow to walk through specifics.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: usage_report_Q2.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick question on pilot supplement credits and billing conversion

Ben — draft playbook attached (pilot_mop_v1.pdf). Key points / recommended defaults: 

• Eligibility: accelerator cohorts and official partners only; must register cohort in HubSpot with sponsor name and cohort dates.
• Credit size cap: default $2,500 per team; escalations for cohorts > 10 teams route to PM + finance.
• Expiration: credits expire 90 days after issuance; conversion to Dedicated allowed once per account and must occur within 60 days of issuance.
• Conversion offer: when converting to Dedicated within 60 days, customer receives a one-time onboarding discount equal to 50% of unused credits applied to first-month usage (cap $10k).
• Accounting/tax guidance: treat these as promotional discounts for revenue recognition (marketing expense) unless total exposure > $25k for a single legal entity — then finance will request escrow/deferral.
• Ops: Billing team should generate a short MOP (attached) and record conversion in HubSpot (deal stage + credit conversion checkbox). Lauren — please confirm the billing run cadence for converted credits and any invoicing caveats.

If SparkFund needs carveouts (e.g., convert > $10k per team), we should require a signed MSA amendment and Finance approval. I added the sample flow and a suggested approval matrix in the attached PDF.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_mop_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kate Morales <kate@pilotlabs.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Shah <ari@sparkfund.co>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on pilot supplement credits and billing conversion

Ben / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the playbook. The eligibility and the 60-day conversion window make sense for our programs. Two follow-ups: 1) can the per-team cap be increased to $5k for flagship finalists (we’ll sponsor the delta), and 2) is the onboarding discount applied as a credit on the first invoice or as an invoice line item reduction?

We’re happy to sign a short amendment if that simplifies approvals. Do you have 20 minutes tomorrow afternoon for a quick alignment call?

—Kate
Head of Programs, Pilot Labs
summary: External partner (SparkFund) asked whether accelerator pilot credits should be treated as promotional vs. deferred revenue and if credits can convert to a Dedicated onboarding discount. Ben looped in Commercial Ops and Finance; Marissa provided a draft playbook (pilot_mop_v1.pdf) with guardrails: eligibility, caps, 60-day conversion window, 90-day expiry, and accounting thresholds (>$25k requires deferral). External asks to increase cap for flagship finalists and confirm invoice mechanics. Next step: 20-minute alignment call and potential MSA amendment.
